correctness.rationale: PASS: four independent atomless finite clocks for two exchangeable collectors of two types give independent fair interval orientations conditional on the unordered pair of arrival times for each type. Direct enumeration of the four orientations for disjoint/crossing/nested endpoint configurations gives respectively 1,1,2 successful paths for one collector, and by exchange symmetry Pr(B)=1/2+(1/2)Pr(nesting). The two nesting directions have probabilities 2 Var(F_2(X)) and 2 Var(F_1(Y)); this proves the exact arbitrary-law identity. For independent X,Y, orthogonal L^2 projections of Z=1{X<Y} onto sigma(X),sigma(Y) bound the variance sum by Var(Z)=p(1-p)<=1/4. Separated-support law F1 uniform(2,3), F2 mixture w uniform(0,1)+(1-w) uniform(4,5), 0<=w<=1/2, attains continuously all 1/2+w(1-w) from 1/2 to 3/4. Exponential substitution yields 1/2+u(u^2+4u+1)/[(u+1)^2(u+2)(2u+1)]; the positive factorization of 2/3 minus this expression is ((u-1)^2(2u^2+7u+2))/(6(u+1)^2(u+2)(2u+1)), hence maximum 2/3 iff equal rates. Independent rational 24-permutation enumeration across 64 integer rate pairs and interval-orientation checks corroborated. No large-type or discrete simultaneous-round assertion follows.
